ios.desc:
NovaScale is a remote-work and server-operations workspace built for Tailscale. Use SSH, monitoring, private web tools, SFTP, Herdr, Remote Git, and Remote Codex from one app—without switching VPN apps.

Built-in Tailscale connects your tailnet inside NovaScale. Traditional SSH hosts and Headscale are also supported.

HOSTS

- Auto-discover tailnet hosts; organize with aliases, icons, groups and pins.

SSH TERMINAL

- Maintained native Swift terminal with customizable themes, external keyboards, combo keys, Simple Commands, OSC52 and Neovim support.

- Pin terminal/tmux sessions; use copy mode with Page Up/Down and choose prefixes such as Ctrl-A. Touch-scroll, click, select and open menus in mouse-aware apps.

- Command/argument suggestions with optional Bash/Zsh integration. Built-in Tailscale handles network changes; recovery depends on network, host and iOS conditions.

REMOTE CODEX

- Install and configure Codex on your host. Threads are managed there; NovaScale is a remote client and may cache content locally for display.

- Connect to your Mac/Linux Codex CLI/app-server via Tailscale. Resume, fork, pin and rename threads; search across projects and sync pins with compatible desktop hosts.

- Send prompts/files, review Markdown, LaTeX and changes, handle approvals, and follow goals, subagents and activity. Adjust text size/spacing; open images full screen.

- Share files directly over authenticated app-server WebSocket; Pro adds linked-host SFTP transfers with byte progress. Diagnose host setup and compatibility in-app.

- Free includes one Codex host, in-app banners and best-effort local notifications.

REMOTE HERDR

- Connect compatible Herdr on Mac/Linux via Tailscale or traditional SSH. Native protocol and controls for workspaces, tabs, agents and status, with a full terminal experience.

- Pin and detach without stopping remote agents; paste images. Free: three daily visits and one pin. Pro: unlimited visits/pins and file/photo uploads.

ON-DEVICE DICTATION

- Dictate in Terminal, Codex and Herdr on supported iOS 26 devices/languages. Works offline after language assets are installed; raw audio is not saved or uploaded.

CODEX & HERDR PUSH

- Optional alerts when remote work needs you, even with NovaScale closed. Choose work opened in NovaScale or selected hosts. Requires host-side setup; plan limits apply. Disable at any time.

REMOTE GIT

- Browse repositories, branches, commits and diffs over SSH. Stage, unstage and commit on the remote host.

quotes.text:
Recently I discovered that Codex CLI ships with an App Server that exposes a WebSocket API. It allows third-party applications to interact with Codex threads, including:

- Resuming existing threads

- Starting new turns

- Handling approval requests

- Receiving thread updates

- Upload small files/images

Since my iOS app(NovaScale, formerly NovaAccess) already includes built-in Tailscale connectivity, connecting it to Codex App Server felt like a natural next step.

The setup is fairly straightforward. A small service running on a Linux or macOS host launches the Codex App Server, generates an authentication token, and exposes the WebSocket endpoint over the Tailnet. NovaScale then connects directly to that endpoint through Tailscale, allowing me to continue Codex work from my phone while away from my desk.

The feature was released last week as part of NovaScale 1.5.0

I also wrote a short technical note explaining how it works and what still needs improvement:

https://galaxnet.dev/nova/articles/remote-codex-in-novascale/

The feature is currently experimental, but it has already become one of my favorite workflows.

Share this for anyone is interested and want a more power rich workflow in a single app.

quotes.text:
I love Tailscale, but I needed to connect to multiple VPN endpoints simultaneously, so I built MintFlow NetStack to solve this issue. However, I still wanted to use Tailscale for easily connecting to my infrastructure servers and homelabs, which created some challenges:

iOS doesn't allow running multiple VPN applications at once
Integrating Tailscale into MintFlow NetStack wasn't feasible because the Go runtime consumes too much memory

So I built NovaAccess to solve this pain point for myself and others facing the same issue. It leverages Tailscale's open-source code and integrates a native SwiftUI SSH terminal into the app. Users can connect to their Tailscale network (tailnet) without running the official Tailscale app – it even works alongside other running VPN applications.
I started considering this idea 10 months ago and decided to build it a month ago. Development went surprisingly well and Apple approved it quickly. AI helped tremendously with the UI work – I never imagined I could complete this app in just one month.

quotes.text:
Hi HN,

I’m an indie developer and heavy Tailscale user. I built NovaAccess because I needed reliable SSH access to my tailnet on iOS without breaking other VPNs.

On iOS, the official Tailscale app requires VPN entitlements, which means you can’t run it alongside another VPN. That was a deal-breaker for my workflow. NovaAccess uses libtailscale directly, so it works without requesting VPN permissions and can coexist with any VPN you’re already using.

What NovaAccess does:

Native SSH terminal for tailnet hosts (SwiftTerm, not WebKit)

Auto-discovery of tailnet nodes

SSH key management

Optional support for custom login servers / Headscale

In the latest update (v1.1.0), I focused heavily on terminal UX and reliability:

Reworked terminal core and accessory keyboard

Better session resume after backgrounding

UI redesign to make daily ops faster

There’s also a Pro tier for people managing multiple tailnets or doing heavier ops:

Multi-tailnet switching

In-tailnet server monitoring

Internal web access

SFTP file management

The free tier is fully usable for SSH access.

I built this primarily for myself and am now trying to see if it’s useful to others.

Feedback (especially critical) is very welcome.
